title: inductor: Fall back to ATen for torch.cat with symbolic non-leading dims
body:
Fixes #189940

## Description
When the concatenation dimension of `torch.cat` is a runtime symint (i.e., a non-leading dim is marked dynamic), Inductor lowers it to a fused `pointwise_cat` kernel. This generates per-element indexing containing modulo/division by a runtime symint (`xindex % ks0`, `xindex // ks0`). GPUs cannot strength-reduce division by a runtime value, making the compiled kernel severely ALU-bound and ~2-2.5x slower than the eager ATen execution on hardware like H100.

**What changed:**
* Added a new config flag `fallback_dynamic_cat` (default `True`).
* Modified `cat` lowering in `torch/_inductor/lowering.py` to route the operation to the ATen fallback handler whenever a non-leading dimension is symbolic. 
* Added a regression test `test_dynamic_cat_non_leading_dim_fallback` to ensure correct behavior with dynamic shapes.

This avoids the expensive symbolic `int64` div/mod in the generated Triton kernel, restoring the bandwidth-bound performance. Local benchmarking confirms the compiled execution time is now on par with eager mode.

## Testing
* Passed local linting (`lintrunner -a`).
* Passed `pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor_dynamic_shapes.py -k "test_dynamic_cat_non_leading_dim_fallback"` on both CUDA and CPU.
